design: Bucknard pre-roll commitment uses expectation across 1-4 outcomes rather than realized die; limited candidate beam-policy search

methods.blind_T2: Search T1-T2 with Bucknard activations withheld; collect highest ranked eligible states (max 4 per turn); choose a single state maximizing mean success over rolls 1,2,3,4; only after roll permit adaptations. Mulligans evaluated assuming neutral 2 Treasures.
methods.neutral_fixed2: Full original T1-T3 solver and mulligan policy with Bucknard deterministically creating 2 Treasures (no random-state roll fishing). This is a stress test, not d4 expected value.
methods.baseline: Original Oct 16 World Map deck, exact matching game IDs and initial shuffle seeds.

limitations: Blind policy is approximate top-K chance-aware candidate search, not exact full imperfect-information solver
Candidate selection uses known library order already present in old goldfish; does not separately blind future draws
After first activation of Bucknard, postroll beam search is adaptive as it should be
Additional copied Bucknard activations after the first use the same forced outcome, a rare approximation
No opponent interaction or post-Dack win-line proof
Partial expected-success outcomes are averaged over four die faces and paired with original binary baseline
